title: eBPF/conntrack upgrade caused cross-AZ control-plane connectivity stalls in Private VPCs
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Follow-up ticket for incident where a routine Private/VPC runtime upgrade that enabled an eBPF-based datapath module triggered mass conntrack table flushes and asymmetric packet handling across AZs, stalling control-plane API requests for several customer VPCs during the upgrade window.
incident_summary: During the 2025-02-20 Private runtime upgrade, the datapath change replacing legacy kube-proxy iptables rules with an eBPF module caused a simultaneous conntrack table reset on a subset of nodes. This produced transient asymmetric routing and TCP resets between control-plane proxies and customer worker nodes across AZ boundaries, resulting in elevated 5xx rates and API timeouts for hosted Private control planes. Impact window: ~27 minutes for most affected VPCs; 3 customers had degraded traffic >45 minutes due to delayed failover to secondary control-plane replicas.
timeline: 2025-02-20T02:14Z - Upgrade rollout started for private-runtime v2.3.1 to enable eBPF datapath
2025-02-20T02:41Z - Alert: control-plane API error rate spike (10x) in us-west-2 cluster group
2025-02-20T02:45Z - Pager duty: oncall SRE traces to increased TCP RSTs and conntrack entries flushing
2025-02-20T02:49Z - Rollback initiated for in-flight nodes after confirmation of conntrack flush behavior
2025-02-20T02:58Z - Rollback complete for initial canary pool; customer-facing errors start declining
2025-02-20T03:11Z - Global mitigation: pause rollout, mark release candidate as blocked, begin deeper RCA
2025-02-20T03:40Z - Engineering confirms root cause and schedules targeted fixes and hardened preflight checks
root_cause: A change in the eBPF datapath update triggered an on-rollout conntrack table reconciliation code path that performed an aggressive global conntrack flush under specific kernel/netfilter conditions present in some underlying AMI images. This flush, combined with asymmetric routing changes introduced by the eBPF program, caused established TCP sessions to be dropped while control-plane proxies were actively reconfiguring, preventing quick reestablishment and resulting in prolonged API request failures until nodes completed rollback/reconnect.
mitigation_taken: Immediate: halted the upgrade rollout and rolled back upgraded nodes back to iptables datapath within the first 15m of detection
Enabled temporary per-node connection draining (extended 120s) to allow control-plane connections to gracefully close before datapath switch
Communicated to affected customers with status updates and incident timeline via support and account teams
postmortem_findings: Upgrade preflight lacked a specific conntrack/iptables compatibility check for the combination of kernel versions and AMI customizations we run in some Private regions
Our canary pool size and sampling did not capture cross-AZ asymmetric routing cases because canaries were co-located in the same AZs as control-plane replicas
Runbooks did not include an immediate diagnostic that enumerates conntrack flush events across nodes or automates rollback when RST spikes exceed threshold
Observability gap: no dedicated metric for ‘conntrack flush count’ emitted to platform dashboards; we relied on downstream symptoms (5xx rate) which delayed root cause correlation
action_items: A1: Add a preflight check that validates kernel/netfilter behavior and simulates a datapath switch on a representative image - owner: Marco Hernandez - estimate 3 - due 2025-03-05
A2: Expand canary strategy to cross-AZ canaries that exercise inter-AZ control-plane traffic patterns - owner: SRE team (lead: Priya Rao) - estimate 2 - due 2025-03-12

A3: Instrument conntrack-related kernel events and emit a 'conntrack_flush_count' metric to the console / alerting pipeline - owner: Runtime Observability (lead: Jin Park) - estimate 3 - due 2025-03-07
A4: Update upgrade runbook to include automated rollback trigger on conntrack_flush_count OR TCP RST spike > 300 within 5 minutes - owner: Runbooks WG - estimate 1 - due 2025-03-03

A5: Revert and rework the eBPF datapath change to avoid global conntrack clears; add a staged patch that performs per-namespace conntrack reconciliation - owner: Runtime Networking (lead: Marco Hernandez) - estimate 5 - due 2025-03-19
A6: Add end-to-end integration test in CI that reproduces the datapath switch under simulated multi-AZ routing and long-lived TCP sessions - owner: QA (lead: Lina Gomez) - estimate 3 - due 2025-03-10
A7: Customer outreach retrospective doc and technical mitigation notes for the three most impacted customers - owner: Customer Success (lead: Elena Rossi) - estimate 1 - due 2025-03-06
status_updates: 2025-02-21: Initial RCA drafted; rollback and immediate mitigations validated in staging; canary strategy review scheduled
2025-02-25: Prototype preflight checks merged to staging; metrics schema for conntrack events approved
2025-03-01: Cross-AZ canary plan approved by SRE; infra tickets created to provision canary VPCs
2025-03-05: Implementing automated alerting for conntrack_flush_count; A1 and A3 in active development
notes: Trade-offs considered: delaying the eBPF rollout across all Private customers would increase technical debt and block egress optimizations; we decided to tighten preflight and canary scope instead.

We evaluated an alternative patch that traps conntrack flushes and drains connections at the socket layer, but that approach added unacceptable complexity for in-flight connections and was deprioritized.
We will schedule a customer webinar to go over the remediation and safe upgrade practices for Private customers who manage custom AMIs
